Stacking just seems unrealistic when you can have 20 units in one tile squeezing through the one tile gap in a civ's mountain borders (which a lot of people complain about, but that's silly; the bottlenecking is meant to be a strategic defense). It completely misses the mark on realism and strategy. Being forced to strategically map out your attacking fronts and the lines in which different units attack from makes perfect sense.

Civ 4 fans are too elitist. The game was great for its time, but Civ 5 really expanded on the weak points and made it stable. Only thing I can really say Civ 4 did better was AI and diplomacy (and perhaps religion).
Stacking had problems, but 1upt was like chopping off a hand to "cure" a broken finger. Fall From Heaven 2 showed how to fix stacking's problems without introducing the idiocy of 1upt.
I never got a chance to mod Civ 4 but holy shit, that mod looks amazing. Might have to give it a try.

I highly recommend it. The civs are all pretty unique, and the religions allow you to shape your playstyle further.

Amurites with a rush for firebows is a decently easy first game, and will help you get acquainted with the wizardly magic system. (There's also religious magic, but it's simpler)

Oh, as for HOW FFH2 dealt with stacking, it used several methods. The ones available to everyone pretty early on are collateral damage units, which damage every unit in a stack. (Civ 4 had these as well, but they were limited to siege weapons IIRC.) The Amurite Firebow I mentioned in my other comment is a good early example. It has a decent defense like any longbow unit will, but it also has the ability to summon fireballs, which are units that last one turn, die after attacking, and hit every enemy in a stack. They can summon 1 per turn

There are AoE spells for some religious units that can hit every unit in multiple tiles at once. The Octopus Overlords and The Ashen Veil religions both get AoE spells on their tier 2 disciple units.

The Sheaim have a unit called the pyre zombie, which only attacks one unit in a stack at a time, and is pretty weak as well, BUT, when it dies it explodes and damages every surrounding tile.

The recon units can get a promotion called marksman, which makes them attack the weakest defender in a stack instead of the standard strongest. (this is amazing for killing enemy support units such as mages or priests)

There might be a few others I'm forgetting, but they add up to making stacks a weakness as well as a strength.
